name: Vincent Jeanbrun
party: Les Republicains (LR) - membership suspended/withdrawn in October 2025 after he joined the second Lecornu government, which LR officially refused to enter
bio: Vincent Jeanbrun, born 5 May 1984 in Paris, is a French politician who has served as Minister of the City and Housing (Ministre de la Ville et du Logement) in the government of Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu since 12 October 2025, a post he retained after the 26 February 2026 reshuffle. The son of a delivery driver and an Italian stay-at-home mother, he grew up in social housing in L'Hay-les-Roses (Val-de-Marne). A member of the youth wing of the UMP from 2004, he became a parliamentary assistant to Valerie Pecresse in 2012. In 2014, aged 29, he was elected mayor of L'Hay-les-Roses, becoming one of the youngest mayors of a French town of more than 30,000 inhabitants; he was re-elected in 2020 and held the office until October 2024. He sat on the Departmental Council of Val-de-Marne (2015) and has been a regional councillor of Ile-de-France since 2015/2021, leading the majority group. He was elected deputy for Val-de-Marne's 7th constituency in the July 2024 snap election, defeating Rachel Keke. A member of Les Republicains, he was suspended/expelled from the party in October 2025 for joining the second Lecornu government. As minister he is associated with the 'statut du bailleur prive' rental-investment incentive (the 'dispositif Jeanbrun'). On 2 July 2023, during the riots following the killing of Nahel Merzouk, his family home was attacked with a burning car driven into the property; his wife and a child were injured fleeing. He is also the subject of a judicial investigation opened in 2024 for suspected illegal taking of interest (prise illegale d'interets).
